events.title: Totila's Ostrogoths take Rome
events.description: After a long siege, the Ostrogothic king Totila entered Rome when Isaurian guards opened a gate. The city, fought over repeatedly in Justinian's Gothic War, was left largely depopulated.
events.html: After a long siege, the Ostrogothic king Totila entered Rome when Isaurian guards opened a gate. The city, fought over repeatedly in Justinian's Gothic War, was left largely depopulated.

events.title: Pope Paul III excommunicates Henry VIII
events.description: Pope Paul III published the bull of excommunication against Henry VIII, prepared in 1535 but suspended. It came after Henry's agents destroyed the shrine of Thomas Becket at Canterbury.

events.title: The Wright brothers make the first powered flights
events.description: At Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds and about 37 metres. Of four flights that day, Wilbur's longest lasted 59 seconds.
events.html: At Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds and about 37 metres. Of four flights that day, Wilbur's longest lasted 59 seconds.

events.title: The Graf Spee is scuttled off Montevideo
events.description: Believing a superior British force waited outside, Captain Hans Langsdorff scuttled the Admiral Graf Spee in the River Plate. He took his own life three days later.
events.html: Believing a superior British force waited outside, Captain Hans Langsdorff scuttled the Admiral Graf Spee in the River Plate. He took his own life three days later.

events.title: The Simpsons premieres as a series
events.description: Fox broadcast the first full episode of The Simpsons, a Christmas special. It became the longest-running American animated series and scripted primetime show.
